talk: Investors judge a growing company on two numbers: how many months of cash are left, and how much cash it burns to add each dollar of new yearly revenue. That second number is the burn multiple: under 1 is excellent, over 2 is a warning sign. Raise money while you still have time, not when you're desperate.

terms.meaning: Cash going out minus cash coming in, per month.
Cash divided by monthly burn: the months you have left.
Cash burned divided by new yearly revenue added.

questions.prompt: The club's new streaming app burns $200,000 a month and has $3M in the bank. How many months of runway?
whyNot: 12 x $200,000 = $2.4M. You'd still have money left.

questions.prompt: Over the year the app burned $2.4M and added $1.6M of new yearly subscription revenue. What's the burn multiple?
questions.hint: Burn divided by new yearly revenue.
working: You burn $1.50 for every $1 of new yearly revenue. Between 1 and 2 is OK, not great.
whyNot: $1.6M / $2.4M = about 0.67 is upside down. Burn goes on top.
$2.4M is the burn, not the ratio.

questions.prompt: You have 15 months of runway and raising money usually takes about 6 months. When should you start?
options: Around month 3, with lots of runway left
questions.hint: Raises slip. Investors can smell desperation.
working: 15 - 6 = 9, so month 9 is the very latest, if nothing slips.
Start around month 3, with 15 - 3 = 12 months left, and you negotiate from strength.
whyNot: Month 9 is the last possible moment, if nothing slips. Something always slips.
With 15 - 14 = 1 month left, investors know you're desperate. The terms get worse.
Too late. No cash means no wages.

penalty.prompt: Over a year the app burned {burn} and added {added} of new yearly revenue. What's the burn multiple?
penalty.hint: Burn divided by new yearly revenue.

traps.why: Upside down. Divide the burn by the new revenue.

call.title: When to raise
call.prompt: The club's app burns $200,000 a month with 15 months of runway. You can cut its marketing by $50,000 a month, saving 12 x $50,000 = $600,000 a year, but slowing growth by about 200 fans a match. Or raise $2M now by selling 10%. Or keep spending and raise later.

options.label: Cut marketing
options.result: Saving $600,000 a year helps, but slower growth costs 200 x $18 = $3,600 every matchday.

options.label: Raise $2M now for 10%
options.result: Good call. Raising with 15 months left means you set the terms. $2M for 10% values the club at $2M / 10% = $20M.

options.label: Keep spending, raise later
options.result: Waiting until cash is short is how founders end up selling a bigger slice for the same money.

later.text: Cash is running low. The only offer is $2M for 25% of the club.

takeaway: Raise while you have runway. A burn multiple under 2 keeps investors interested.
